draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Mahabalipuram! This was one of the two big port cities of the Pallava kingdom, and in the 7th and 8th centuries its kings had whole temples carved out of the living rock. Those monuments are now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and you're standing right among them.
draft.hungryLine: Grab a cheap big breakfast at the stalls on the road down to the Shore Temple, drink a fresh coconut by the monuments, and pick your own grilled fish for dinner.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Krishna's Butterball is a 2 min walk, Arjuna's Penance is 3 minutes away, and the Sthalasayana Perumal Temple is about 4 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head down and chill on the sandy beach, or catch a morning yoga class in town.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The five rathas were never consecrated as temples, because work stopped when King Narasimhavarman I died.

spots.name: Krishna's Butterball
spots.detail: 2 min walk · A giant granite boulder balanced on a slope

spots.name: Arjuna's Penance
spots.detail: 3 min walk · One of the largest open-air rock reliefs in the world

spots.name: Sthalasayana Perumal Temple
spots.detail: 4 min walk · One of the 108 Divya Desams, said to be the birthplace of the saint Bhoothathalvar

legends.title: The Seven Pagodas
legends.body: For over eleven centuries people have told of six more temples that once stood by the sea alongside the Shore Temple. That's why the early Europeans nicknamed the town the Seven Pagodas.

tips.title: Get your tickets before 5:30PM.
tips.body: The ticket counter for the Shore Temple, caves and Five Rathas closes at 5:30PM and entry ends at 6PM, and one ticket covers all the monuments for the day.

tips.title: Keep the camera down at the old lighthouse.
tips.body: Photography is not allowed at the Olakkannesvara Temple because it's in a high-security zone near a nuclear power station.

story.title: A port the Greeks knew
story.body: The earliest mention of the town is in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, written by an unknown Greek navigator. Ptolemy called it Malange.

story.title: Temples cut from rock
story.body: Under Mahendravarman I and his son Narasimhavarman I, also called Mamalla, the rathas were carved from single blocks of granite. The town is named after Mamalla.

story.title: The Shore Temple
story.body: Narasimhavarman II built the Shore Temple from granite blocks while this was still a busy port. It's one of the oldest structural stone temples in South India.

story.title: Later hands
story.body: In the 16th century the Vijayanagara Empire enclosed the old Krishna relief inside a mandapa. The British laid out the modern town plan in 1827.

story.title: World Heritage
story.body: The monuments were restored after 1960 and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984. Today the town is famous for its stone carvings.
